page: OVHcloud b3-512-flex is a general-purpose cloud server powered by AMD EPYC processors running on KVM virtualization. The configuration supplies 128 dedicated x86_64 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz, configured with one thread per core without hyperthreading. Memory capacity is 512 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes a compact 50 GB local NVMe SSD, baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps, and does not include complementary public IPv4 addresses or discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong multi-threaded compute and memory capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier multi-core stress-ng rating of 288,676.35 and processed 161.2 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reached 10,338.65 GB/sec on small cached read operations and sustained 273.56 GB/sec on large uncached read transfers. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 1,143.25 GB/sec, placing it in the upper decile, while static web serving throughput reached 61.45 GB/sec.

The primary architectural tradeoff lies between computational density and local disk capacity. While the dedicated 128-core topology and 512 GB memory pool provide immense processing density and high memory bandwidth, the included 50 GB NVMe storage is sized strictly for the base operating environment, necessitating external block or object storage for larger persistence layers. Single-threaded metrics, including gzip compression and single-core decompression, deliver middle-tier baseline throughput. This server fits distributed memory caches, parallel batch processing, ETL pipelines, static web distribution nodes, and multi-threaded compilation clusters.
description: OVHcloud b3-512-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform. Operating on KVM virtualization, it provides 128 dedicated physical cores with single-threading running at 2.3 GHz, alongside 512 GB of system RAM matching a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware provisions include a compact 50 GB local NVMe SSD, 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and zero bundled public IPv4 addresses, with no GPU hardware present. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded throughput, reaching 288,676.35 on stress-ng multi-core and 161.2 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-threaded tasks and the modest local disk footprint represent operational boundaries, the server offers dense compute and strong uncached memory bandwidth for highly concurrent workloads. It is suitable for large-scale in-memory caching tiers, intensive batch processing, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving.
